gaps.sentence: If only the government ___ something about housing costs!
gaps.hint: a strong wish for change, would
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus 'would' expresses a strong wish for change: would do.

gaps.sentence: Unless it ___ below five degrees tonight, the event will go ahead.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses take the present simple even when referring to tonight: drops.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ a muscle, apply ice at once.
gaps.hint: medical instruction, present simple after if
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a conditional instruction uses the present simple, never 'will': pull.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me, I would have helped you move house.
gaps.hint: a missed request in the past
gaps.explanation: An unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had asked.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ a million euros, I would travel the world for a year.
gaps.explanation: Second conditionals use the past simple after 'if' for unreal presents: won.

gaps.sentence: I will be surprised if he ___ on time for once.
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the present simple: arrives.

gaps.sentence: Unless the road ___, the coach cannot use this route.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' takes the present simple, here in the passive: is widened.
